title: Suppliers and the supply chain
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-01T09:32:51Z recheck: the fresh check agreed with the fix, cleared with the fix

match.reason: The closest bank point, Customers, suppliers and competitors, covers suppliers only as one of three groups at the right Year 11 depth, and the supply chain card is Year 12 and wider, so neither teaches this point as it is or with small changes.

draft.title: Suppliers and the supply chain
card: Suppliers are the businesses that provide the materials, goods or services a business needs. The supply chain is the path these resources take until they reach the business.
Cost
the prices suppliers charge, and the cost of transport, add to what it costs the business to make or sell its product.
Reliability
if a supplier delivers late or short, the business may run out of stock and lose sales.
Reputation
customers may care how goods are made. A supplier with poor practices can harm the business's reputation.
draft.remember: Suppliers affect a business's cost, reliability and reputation.

a.q: A café's milk supplier often delivers late, so the café sometimes has none. Which part of supplier choice does this show?
opts: Reliability
Cost
Reputation
Location
a.why: Late deliveries mean the café cannot count on getting stock when it needs it, which is a question of reliability. Cost is about prices, not about whether goods arrive on time.
a.clue: The problem is about goods arriving when needed.

b.q: Nina sells T-shirts online from Bendigo. A cheaper supplier has been criticised for poor working conditions. What risk does using it bring?
opts: Harm to her reputation with customers
A rise in the cost of her stock
Late delivery of her stock each week
Fewer choices of stock for her to sell
b.why: Customers may care how goods are made, so a supplier with poor practices can harm Nina's reputation. The supplier is cheaper, so the risk is not a higher cost, and the case says nothing about late delivery.
b.clue: Think about what customers may think of how the shirts are made.

b.best: Harm to her reputation with customers

problems.detail: The card says the supply chain ends when resources reach the business. A supply chain usually runs from raw materials all the way to the final customer, so this definition is narrower than the standard one and could mislead students.

The stem asks which 'part of supplier choice' the case shows, but the card presents cost, reliability and reputation as ways suppliers affect a business, not as parts of supplier choice. Asking which effect of suppliers the case shows would match the card better.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer (Reliability; harm to reputation), and the explanations agree with the card. Minor issues: the card defines the supply chain as ending at the business, which is narrower than the usual definition, and question a's 'part of supplier choice' does not match the card's framing.
